label: Objects
description: Objects. `make` gives a value written in place -- or a value another node answered -- a declared type, so other nodes can read its fields; `merge` lays one object over another.

make.description: The value, as the declared type. Write the object in place: "in": { "value": { "count": "{{count}}", "text": "{{joined}}" }, "type": "@features/f/domain/Digest.shape.json" }; or hand it a value another node answered, to give it a type. A closed type keeps only the fields it declares: an open or wider value -- a row an API answered through an open edge shape -- is narrowed to them here, at every depth, and this is the one place a value is narrowed so; everywhere else a closed type takes only a value of its own fields. The checker verifies the value fits the type once narrowed; at run time the narrowed value is judged against it.

value.description: the object, written in place or read from a node

type.description: the declared type of the result

merge.description: over laid on top of base -- every key of over wins -- as the declared type. Like Object.assign({}, base, over).

type.description: the declared type of the result
